rationale:
Identity was properly verified using full name and zip, matching a single user. The agent fetched order details correctly and acted only on the authenticated user’s orders. It canceled both pending orders and initiated the return for the correct watch item, and the refund totals provided at the end are accurate and supported by tool outputs.

However, the policy requires the agent to state the exact change and obtain explicit confirmation before any action that changes an order. The agent said it would proceed to cancel the two pending orders but did not explicitly request or receive confirmation to cancel them before executing the cancellations. The user only confirmed which watch to return and the refund method. This constitutes performing order-changing writes without explicit confirmation, violating the stated policy. There were also minor non-tool-backed statements (e.g., 5–7 business day refund timing, promise of an email), but the decisive failure is the lack of explicit confirmation before canceling the pending orders.
